_about: Habitat atmospheres used to rank investigations. scripts/build_cards.py counts, per investigation, the tests whose CHAMBER O2 and pressure both fall inside each habitat's 'match' box (burner-stream O2 of inverse flames is never counted: it is gas blown out of the burner, not cabin air). Every value has a source; values that are the team's choice are listed under 'assumptions'. Units: O2 in % by volume, pressure in kPa (1 psi = 6.895 kPa).

challenge.label: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge text (Potential considerations: Spacesuits and oxygen concentration; Partial-gravity data)

ntrs_m2m.label: Walton & Norcross, Moon to Mars (M2M): Exploration Atmosphere, NASA JSC, NTRS 20240003211 (2024), abstract

guide.label: NASA, A Researcher's Guide to Combustion Science (2015)

habitats.label: ISS / spacecraft at sea-level air

sources.quote: the sea level atmosphere of 14.7 psia, 21% oxygen (O2) found on the International Space Station, Shuttle, and most other Russian and Chinese space vehicles and stations
the Earth's pressure at sea level is 14.7 psi

assumptions: The match box (19-24% O2, 90-110 kPa) is the team's tolerance around the 21% / 101.3 kPa target.

habitats.label: Moon habitat & pressurized rover
habitats.gravity: lunar (about 0.16 g): no combustion data at this gravity

sources.quote: The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less.
it is expected that the Moon Base and pressurized rover(s) will be at a pressure and oxygen concentration between those in a spacesuit and the Earth's atmosphere
Current plans for M2M habitats on the Lunar surface require EVA, thus EA recommendation became 8 psia and 32% O2 but was revised to 8.2 psia and 34% O2

assumptions: Moon habitat and rover share one entry because the challenge gives them the same atmosphere.

habitats.label: Mars base (assumed same air as the Moon habitat)
habitats.gravity: Mars (about 0.38 g): no combustion data at this gravity
assumptions: Neither the challenge nor the NTRS abstract gives a Mars atmosphere. The team assumes the same exploration atmosphere as the Moon habitat; show this as an assumption in the UI.

reference_points.label: Spacesuit
reference_points.quote: spacesuits are filled with 100% oxygen to only 4.3 psi

reference_points.label: Shuttle before spacewalks
reference_points.quote: the Shuttle was retroactively certified to operate using 10.2 psia, 26.5% O2

reference_points.label: Skylab
reference_points.quote: changing the atmosphere to 5 psia, 70-74% O2

reference_points.label: Mercury to Apollo
reference_points.quote: Early space vehicles (Mercury through Apollo Programs) used a 5 psia, 100% O2 environment

shared_facts.text: There is currently no partial-gravity combustion data in PSI. Microgravity and normal-gravity results could bound what happens at Moon or Mars gravity.
Partial gravity was mimicked in ACME's E-FIELD Flames experiment through the effect of the electric field on the ions in flames.
Spacecraft ventilation airflow is in the 0-30 cm/s range; solids burn at the lowest oxygen at about 10 cm/s, typical of spacecraft ventilation.
